---
name: or-motion-scene
description: Author, validate and materialise a deterministic MotionScene in the open OR project — code-to-illustration, animated titles, diagrams and reusable scene JSON. Use when the user asks for an illustration, motion graphic or scene from code. Do NOT use for ordinary edits (or-timeline-edit) or for changing OR's own MotionScene implementation.
---

# Motion scene

Workspace guide: `docs/motion-scenes.md`.

## Procedure

1. Decide the input: a source file (code illustration) or an authored
   `.ormotion.json` (title, diagram, reusable scene).
2. For a scene, start from `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs --name "Title"
   --out scenes/title.ormotion.json`, then edit nodes, text, colours, sizes and
   keyframes.
3. Validate with `tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json
   --json`. Fix every diagnostic; do not render a scene that fails validation.
4. Place it with `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene {scene_path}` or `{source_path}`,
   using absolute paths. This is the one insert the CLI cannot do: `tools/or
   motion materialize` only writes a file. Materialisation encodes every frame:
   wait for the result and never run two at once.
5. Verify the clip appears with `tools/or timeline clips --track TRACK_ID
   --attach project.json --json`, then `tools/or project save --attach
   project.json --json` unless the user asked to review first.

## Rules

- The scene is declarative and bounded: no expressions, scripts, network assets
  or provider calls. Refer to assets by scene-local or project-relative path.
- Text is literal; changing the title means changing the `text` field.
- A re-render never replaces the existing clip. Insert the new render and remove
  the old clip only when the user asks.
- Keep scenes short; a long scene is slow to encode and hard to revise.
- A reusable asset is listed with `mcp__or__motion_asset_list`, inserted with
  `mcp__or__motion_asset_insert` (pass parameter values by id) and saved with
  `mcp__or__motion_asset_save` from an authored scene file. Do not copy or edit
  library files yourself.

## Report

State the scene file, its duration and canvas, the track and time the clip was
inserted at, and whether the project was saved.

---
name: or-project-safety
description: Protect the open OR project while editing — check revision and dirty state, save explicitly, undo or redo canonical history through the workspace or CLI, handle refused commands and report honestly. Use before any save, undo or recovery decision, or when a project command fails unexpectedly. Do NOT use for designing OR's history or command model.
---

# Project safety

Workspace guide: `docs/project-safety.md`.

## Procedure

1. Before changing anything, read `tools/or project summary --attach project.json
   --json`.
2. After the requested change, read the affected state (`timeline clips` or
   `media list`).
3. Save once with `tools/or project save --attach project.json --json` unless the
   user asked to review first.
4. If the user wants a change undone, use `tools/or history undo --attach
   project.json --json` and say how many edits it covered. Never close, shut down
   or reset the project.

## Rules

- Never write a `.orproj` file or any project path directly.
- A revision conflict or refused command: re-read, retry once with real values,
  then stop and report.
- `dirty` is evidence. If an edit succeeded but the project is not dirty, report
  the inconsistency instead of claiming success.
- Do not invent command success. Every claim names the verb and the state you read.

description: Make one timeline change in the open OR project through the workspace or CLI — add, insert, move, trim, split, delete, re-time or mark clips, tracks and the sequence. Use when the user asks for an edit to the timeline. Do NOT use for media import (read docs/media-and-import.md), MotionScene authoring (or-motion-scene), or developing OR itself.

# Timeline edit

Workspace guide: `docs/timeline-editing.md`.

## Procedure

1. `tools/or project summary --attach project.json --json` — confirm the project
   and read the revision.
2. `tools/or timeline tracks|settings|markers --attach project.json --json` and
   `tools/or timeline clips --track TRACK_ID` — read rates, tracks, clips and
   markers. Use only ids and times from these results.
3. Choose the smallest command. If the target track does not exist, create it with
   `timeline add-track`; text and caption clips need a text or caption track.
4. Run it with `--attach project.json --json` and exact `NUM/DEN` or decimal times.
5. Re-read the track when placement matters, then `tools/or project save
   --attach project.json --json` unless the user asked to review first.

## Rules

- One requested change per turn; do not bundle unrequested edits.
- Never invent ids or times from the prompt. The panel context names the current
  clip and playhead only when they exist.
- `--mode insert` moves later clips right; `--mode overwrite` clears the range.
  Say which one you used.
- When this workspace has no `project.json` to attach through, use the matching
  `mcp__or__*` tool and say so.
- A refused edit is information: re-read, retry once with valid values, then
  report.

## Report

Name the track, the clip and the exact time that changed, and whether the project
was saved.

# OR Agent Workspace

This is the operating workspace the Opencut Reinforced assistant uses by default.
It is not the OR source checkout. The open project is recorded in `project.json`,
and the `or` CLI attached through that pointer is the default way to read or
change it. An `mcp__or__*` tool is a fallback for the few operations the CLI
cannot express.

## Rule

Read the smallest entry that answers the current task. Do not preload the guides:
each line below names the situation that makes it the right thing to read.

## Routing

### Guides

- **Timeline editing** — tracks, clips, markers and sequence commands with exact times.
  When: the user asks to add, move, trim, split, delete, reorder, re-time or mark something on the timeline.
  Path: `docs/timeline-editing.md`
- **Media and import** — media ids, importing, paging and source relinking.
  When: the task needs a file in the library before it can be placed, or needs an existing media id.
  Path: `docs/media-and-import.md`
- **Motion scenes** — code-to-video scenes, `.ormotion.json`, validation and materialisation.
  When: the user asks for an illustration, motion graphic, animated title or scene from code.
  Path: `docs/motion-scenes.md`
- **Project safety** — revisions, save, undo/redo and refused commands.
  When: deciding whether to save, undoing a change, or recovering from a failed command.
  Path: `docs/project-safety.md`
- **Troubleshooting** — missing tools, no open project, slow or failed renders.
  When: a command fails and the error is not self-explanatory.
  Path: `docs/troubleshooting.md`

### Skills

The session catalog carries these. Load one only when its task matches.

- `or-timeline-edit` — orient, act, verify and save one timeline change.
- `or-motion-scene` — author, validate and materialise a deterministic scene.
- `or-project-safety` — protect revisions and report edits honestly.

### Tools

- `tools/or` — the OR CLI bound to this app build and the default project surface.
  Run it from this workspace: `tools/or <verb> --attach project.json --json`.
  `project.json` is the app-written session pointer; the CLI follows its
  `descriptor_path`, so the same command line keeps working when another project
  opens. `tools/or commands` and `tools/or queries` print the exact verb surface.
- `tools/motion-scaffold.mjs` — writes a valid V1 `.ormotion.json` skeleton:
  `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs --name "Title" --out scenes/title.ormotion.json`.
- `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene`, `mcp__or__motion_asset_list`,
  `mcp__or__motion_asset_insert`, `mcp__or__motion_asset_save` — the app's MCP
  fallback. Use them only for motion insertion and the motion library, where the
  CLI can render a file but cannot import or place a clip. A CLI failure whose
  error does not explain itself is the other fallback; report it before switching.

## Working files

- `scenes/` — scene sources you author. `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene` reads them.
- `work/` — scratch files, notes and copies. Nothing here is project state.
- `project.json`, `or-cli.json` and `tools/or` are written by the app; leave them
  alone. `project.json` names the live descriptor the CLI attaches through.

## Bounds

- Never edit a `.orproj` file, the project directory, or any path listed in `project.json`.
- Project mutations go through `tools/or ... --attach project.json`; the app applies
  them and owns history. The motion MCP tools are the only other write path.
- Make one requested change at a time, confirm it with a timeline read, then save
  unless the user asked to review first.

# Media and import

Scope: getting a file into the project library and finding the id that the
timeline commands take. The library is project state; importing is a project
mutation and is saved like any other edit.

## Order of operations

1. `tools/or media list --attach project.json --json` — check whether the file is
   already imported. The list is paged: pass `--offset` while the page reports
   more items.
2. `tools/or media add --attach project.json --source PATH --json` — import an
   **absolute** path. The result carries the new media id and its metadata.
3. Place it with `timeline insert-clip` (see
   [timeline-editing.md](timeline-editing.md)); use the duration from this result.
4. `tools/or project save --attach project.json --json` after the edit, unless the
   user asked to review first.

## What can be imported

- Video, audio and image files that the app's FFmpeg build decodes.
- A file must exist and be readable when `media add` runs; the library records a
  source path, not a copy.
- Importing the same path twice is allowed; use the id the new call returns.

## Paths

- `--source` must be absolute. The workspace sits outside the project, so a path
  relative to the project is not automatically correct.
- Files the agent downloaded or wrote live under `work/`; copy or keep them there
  and pass that absolute path.
- Do not move or delete a source file after importing it. If it moves, relink it:
  `tools/or media relink --attach project.json --id MEDIA_ID --source PATH --json`.
- `tools/or media remove --attach project.json --id MEDIA_ID --json` removes a
  library entry when the user asks for it.

## Reading metadata

`media list` returns ids, source paths and duration metadata. Use the returned
duration when a clip needs a length; do not round it into a different time base.
`project summary` reports the project revision and dirty state.

# Motion scenes

Scope: turning code or a declarative `.ormotion.json` scene into an ordinary,
editable video clip through the app's deterministic MotionScene renderer. No
provider or network call happens here.

## Two inputs

| Input | Use |
|---|---|
| A source file | `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene {source_path: "<absolute path>/work/sample.rs"}` turns the code into a highlighted illustration. |
| A scene file | `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene {scene_path: "<absolute path>/scenes/title.ormotion.json"}` renders an authored scene. |

Pass exactly one of `source_path` and `scene_path`, as absolute paths. The call
materialises video frames through the app, imports the result and inserts an
ordinary clip. It is the one project operation the CLI cannot do: `tools/or
motion materialize` only writes a file. It is slow because every frame is
encoded; do not start a second render while one is running and do not retry after
a timeout without checking the timeline.

Useful optional arguments: `title`, `at`, `track_id`, `width`, `height`,
`frame_rate` (`30/1`), `output_path`. When `at` is omitted the clip is appended
after the target track; when `track_id` is omitted the first video track is used.

## Authoring a scene

Start from the scaffold, then edit the JSON:

```sh
node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs --name "Title" --out scenes/title.ormotion.json
```

Validate before rendering:

```sh
tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
```

`tools/or motion inspect` summarises nodes and animation counts;
`tools/or motion evaluate --file ... --at 1/2` shows the resolved instructions at
one exact time and touches neither a project nor the encoder. `tools/or motion
render` rasterises one frame to a PNG when a still is enough. `tools/or motion
from-code` writes a scene from a source file without materialising it, so the
agent can adjust the generated scene first.

`tools/or motion materialize --attach project.json --source PATH --output
<absolute .mkv>` renders to disk through the live app but does not import or
insert the result; use it only when a file is wanted, never as an insertion path.

## Envelope

```json
{
  "format": "opencut-reinforced-motion-scene",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "scene_id": "<UUIDv4>",
  "name": "...",
  "duration": {"numerator": 4, "denominator": 1},
  "canvas": {"width": 1920, "height": 1080},
  "assets": [],
  "nodes": [],
  "animations": []
}
```

Node kinds: `group`, `text`, `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `arrow`, `image`.

- Text needs `text`; optional `position`, `font_size`, `fill`, `spans`
  (byte-offset highlight runs).
- Rectangle and ellipse need `size`; optional `position`, `fill`, `stroke`,
  `stroke_width`, `rotation_degrees`, `opacity`.
- Image needs `asset_id`; group needs `children`.
- Colours are typed `{red, green, blue, alpha}` with 0–255 channels. There is no
  CSS string and no expression language.
- Animated properties are `translation_x`, `translation_y`, `scale`, `rotation`,
  `opacity`, `width`, `height`. Keyframes are ascending, inside `[0, duration]`,
  and each node animates a property once. Easings: `linear`, `ease_in`,
  `ease_out`, `ease_in_out`.

To change the title, a colour or a size, edit the node's fields and re-materialise.
The materialised clip already on the timeline is an ordinary video clip; re-running
the scene never silently replaces it — insert the new render and delete the old
clip only if the user asks.

## Reusable assets

The app has an asset library (ADR 0010): reusable scenes, fragments and image
cutouts with typed parameters for text, colour, size, opacity and rotation. This
is the second fallback surface; the CLI asset verbs need a library folder path
this workspace does not expose, so use the app's MCP tools, not the file system:

- `mcp__or__motion_asset_list` — ids, names, categories, kinds and durations.
- `mcp__or__motion_asset_insert` — instantiate one asset with a `values` object
  keyed by parameter id, render it through the app, and insert an ordinary clip.
  Text and choice values are strings, numbers are numbers, and colours are
  `{red,green,blue,alpha}`.
- `mcp__or__motion_asset_save` — save an authored `.ormotion.json` scene as a
  reusable, classified library asset with a preview.

When the user names a library folder and only wants inspection, the CLI can read
it: `tools/or motion asset list --library PATH --json`.

## Bounds

A scene file is at most 4 MiB, 4096 nodes, groups nested 16 deep, 4096
animations, 4096 keyframes per animation, 64 KiB per text node. Asset paths must
be scene-local or project-relative; remote URLs are refused. Keep scenes short:
a ten-second 30 fps scene is 300 encoded frames.

# Project safety

Scope: how to change a live project without losing work. Rust owns the project,
its revision and its history; every `tools/or` mutation goes through the same
validated command path as the editor.

## The one rule

Never edit a `.orproj` file or anything inside the project directory directly.
The running app holds the authoritative document; a direct edit is invisible to
it and will be overwritten or rejected. Attach through `project.json` and let the
app apply the command.

## Reading state

`tools/or project summary --attach project.json --json` returns the project name,
file, revision and dirty state. `timeline` queries and `media list` are reads:
they never mutate.

Edits are live in the app as soon as the command succeeds, but they are unsaved
until `project save` runs. `dirty: false` after an edit means something is wrong;
report it instead of claiming success.

## Save and history

- Call `tools/or project save --attach project.json --json` once after finishing
  the requested change, unless the user asked to review first.
- `tools/or history undo --attach project.json --json` and
  `tools/or history redo --attach project.json --json` are the canonical history.
  They undo one project edit, not one conversation turn; tell the user how many
  steps you undid.
- Never call a session or recovery shutdown. Closing the app is the user's action.

## Refused operations

A refused command is a real answer, not a transient error:

- A time outside the sequence or a trim that inverts a clip: re-read the
  timeline and choose a valid time.
- A revision conflict: re-read `project summary`, then repeat the edit once.
- A duplicate id or a missing media id: re-read ids and retry with real values.

Do not loop on the same failing command. After two identical failures, stop and
report the verb, its error code and the next concrete step.

## Reporting

Say what changed: track, clip, exact time. Say what was saved. Do not claim a
change that no command confirmed; a timeline read after the edit is the minimum
evidence.

# Timeline editing

Scope: the exact-time timeline commands the assistant runs against the live
project. Project state is Rust-owned; read [project-safety.md](project-safety.md)
before saving or undoing.

## Order of operations

1. `tools/or project summary --attach project.json --json` — confirm a project is
   open and read its revision and dirty state.
2. `tools/or timeline tracks --attach project.json --json` and
   `tools/or timeline settings --attach project.json --json` — read the track ids
   and the sequence rate.
3. `tools/or timeline clips --track TRACK_ID --attach project.json --json` — read
   the clips with their start, source range and duration. Page with `--offset`
   and `--limit` when the page reports more.
4. Use only the ids and times those calls returned. Never invent a `clip_id`,
   `track_id` or media id.
5. Make the smallest command the request needs.
6. Re-read the affected track when placement matters.
7. `tools/or project save --attach project.json --json` unless the user asked to
   review first.

## Time form

- Times are exact `NUM/DEN` seconds or decimal seconds (`2.5`).
- A clip's `--at` is its timeline start; `--source-start` addresses the media
  in-point.
- `insert-clip` has no default duration: pass `--duration` taken from the media
  metadata in [media-and-import.md](media-and-import.md).
- Do not guess a position from the prompt. The panel sends the selected clip and
  playhead as context when they exist; otherwise ask or append after the last clip.

## Commands

Every command below takes `--attach project.json --json` plus the flags shown.

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `timeline add-track --kind video\|audio\|text\|caption` | Add an empty track. |
| `timeline insert-clip --track --media --at --source-start --duration` | Place imported media at an exact time. `--mode insert` (the default) moves later clips right; `--mode overwrite` clears the range. |
| `timeline insert-text --track --at --duration --text` | Add a text clip; `insert-caption` adds a caption clip instead. |
| `timeline move-clip --clip --track --at` | Move a clip in time, possibly to another track. |
| `timeline trim-clip --clip --edge start\|end --to` | Trim one edge to an exact timeline time; `--ripple` closes the gap. |
| `timeline split-clip --clip --at` | Split a clip; the right-hand part starts there. |
| `timeline delete-clip --clip` | Delete a clip and leave the gap. |
| `timeline ripple-delete-clip --clip` | Delete a clip and close the gap on that track. |
| `timeline set-frame-rate --rate NUM/DEN` | Set the sequence rate; `clear-frame-rate` unsets it. |
| `timeline add-marker --at --label` | Add a labelled marker. |

`tools/or commands` lists every mutating verb and `tools/or queries` lists every
read, with their schema versions, when the exact surface is not obvious.

## Track and clip rules

- Visual tracks (`video`, `text`, `caption`) carry visual clips; `audio` tracks
  carry audio clips. A text clip on a video track is refused.
- Text and caption clips need a text or caption track; create one with `add-track`
  when the timeline has none.
- Clips cannot overlap on one track. `insert` makes room, `overwrite` replaces it.
- Track order on screen is the order `timeline tracks` returns.

## Examples

Append a clip to the end of the first video track:

1. `media list` → choose the media id; `timeline clips --track TRACK_ID` → read
   the track's last clip end.
2. `timeline insert-clip --track TRACK_ID --media MEDIA_ID --at "<end>"
   --source-start 0 --duration "<media duration>"`.
3. `timeline clips --track TRACK_ID`, then `project save`.

Trim the selected clip to end at 4 s:

1. The panel context names the clip and its track.
2. `timeline trim-clip --clip CLIP_ID --edge end --to 4`.
3. Verify the duration is positive; a trim that would invert the clip is refused.

# Troubleshooting

Scope: the failures the assistant can meet inside this workspace, and the next
concrete step for each. Report the cause, never a guessed success.

## `tools/or` is missing or not executable

The app writes `tools/or` when it connects to the app build. If it is absent, the
assistant cannot reach the project through the CLI. Check `or-cli.json` for the
path the app recorded, and tell the user to reconnect the assistant. Do not write
your own bridge or edit the project files.

## `--attach project.json` fails

The CLI reports that no project is open or that the endpoint is unavailable. The
app has no open project, the project.json pointer is stale, or this session is
not using the agent workspace (a project-folder or chosen-folder workspace has no
pointer to attach through).

- Ask the user to open or create a project in OR, then retry once.
- When this workspace has no `project.json`, use the `mcp__or__*` tools for the
  edit instead, and say which surface you used.

## A motion MCP tool is not available

`mcp__or__motion_insert_scene` and the motion asset tools come from the app's MCP
server. If the session does not expose them, the CLI can still validate and
render a scene file to disk, but it cannot import or insert the result. Tell the
user that insertion needs the app's assistant connection, and stop there.

## Materialisation is slow

`motion_insert_scene` encodes every frame with the app's encoder. A short scene
still takes seconds to minutes. Wait for the tool result; do not start a second
render and do not retry after a timeout without checking whether the clip
appeared. If a render fails, read the returned code, fix the scene, and retry
once.

## Scene validation codes

Common codes and their fix:

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `MOTION_INVALID_SCENE_ID` | `scene_id` must be a fresh UUIDv4. |
| `MOTION_INVALID_DURATION` | `duration` must be greater than zero. |
| `MOTION_MISSING_TEXT` / `MOTION_MISSING_SIZE` | Add the field the node kind requires. |
| `MOTION_KEYFRAMES_UNSORTED` / `MOTION_KEYFRAME_OUT_OF_RANGE` | Sort keyframes and keep them inside the duration. |
| `MOTION_ANIMATION_UNKNOWN_NODE` | The `node_id` must exist in `nodes`. |
| `MOTION_REMOTE_ASSET_REFUSED` | Use a scene-local or project-relative asset path. |

## A command is refused

See [project-safety.md](project-safety.md). Re-read state, retry once with real
ids and times, then report the refusal if it repeats.

# Workspace tools

Scope: the local commands this workspace exposes. `tools/or` is the default way
to read and change the open project; `mcp__or__*` tools are the fallback for
motion insertion and the motion library.

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `tools/or <verb> --attach project.json --json` | The OR CLI bound to the running app build. Reads and edits the live project through the app-written pointer. `tools/or commands` and `tools/or queries` list the verbs. |
| `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs` | Write a valid V1 `.ormotion.json` skeleton into `scenes/`. |
| `tools/or motion ...` | Validate, inspect, evaluate, render or write a scene file; none of these inserts a clip. |
| `tools/or motion asset ...` | Inspect a motion library folder the user names. |

## Examples

```sh
tools/or project summary --attach project.json --json
tools/or timeline tracks --attach project.json --json
tools/or timeline clips --track TRACK_ID --attach project.json --json
tools/or media list --attach project.json --json
tools/or project save --attach project.json --json
tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion inspect --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion evaluate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --at 1/2 --json
tools/or motion from-code --source work/sample.rs --output scenes/sample.ormotion.json
tools/or motion render --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --at 1/2 --output work/title.png
tools/or motion asset list --library work/motion-library --json
```

`motion materialize` needs a live app but only writes the output file. To place a
scene on the timeline, use `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene`; it renders, imports and
inserts in one call.

## Bounds

- `tools/or` is written by the app on connect; editing it is pointless.
- Scaffold and CLI write only the files you name; nothing else is project state.
